Rashi on Chullin 5a:10:1.hebrew: מכם - אדם כי יקריב מכם קרבן, וגבי נדר או נדבה כתיב, דהא כי יקריב משמע כשירצו להקריב:
Rashi on Chullin 5a:10:1.english: From you - [The verse] "When a man from among you brings an offering" is written with regard to a vow or a voluntary offering, for the expression "when he brings" implies [a case] when they wish to bring [it].

Rashi on Chullin 5a:10:2.english: To exclude the apostate - for we do not accept his donation.

Rashi on Chullin 5a:10:3.hebrew: מכם בכם חילקתי - כלומר, מדכתיב האי מיעוטא בישראל ולא באומות, דכתיב איש איש מבית ישראל אשר יקריב קרבן לכל נדריכם וגו' בפרשת מומין (ויקרא כב), ותניא לקמן בפירקין (חולין דף יג:): איש, מה תלמוד לומר איש איש? לרבות העובדי כוכבים שנודרים נדרים ונדבות כישראל, וגבי דידהו לא כתיב מיעוטא, דלכתוב מן האדם כי יקריב קרבן, דמשמע ולא כל האדם. שמע מינה: בכם חלקתי, שכשרין מביאין ולא המומרין, ולא באומות, שכולן מתנדבין מקבלין מהם:
Rashi on Chullin 5a:10:3.english: "Of you" - "among you I have distinguished" - That is to say: since this exclusion is written with regard to Israel and not with regard to the nations - for it is written, "Any man of the house of Israel...who offers his sacrifice for any of their vows, etc." (Leviticus 22), in the section dealing with blemishes, and it is taught further on in this chapter (Chullin 13b): "man" (ish) - why does it say "any man" (ish ish)? To include idolaters, who make vows and freewill-offerings just as an Israelite does. But regarding them no exclusion is written, for had it meant to exclude, it should have written "when a man of mankind (min ha-adam) shall offer a sacrifice," which would imply "and not all mankind." From this we learn: "among you I have distinguished" - [only] fit [Israelites] may bring offerings, and not apostates; but this is not so regarding the nations, for whichever of them makes a donation, it is accepted from him.

Rashi on Chullin 5a:10:4.hebrew: עם הדומה לבהמה - שאין מקיימין את המצות, מן דכתיב גבי בהמה למעוטי רובע ונרבע, הכי דריש ליה בבבא קמא (דף מ:) ובבכורות (דף מא.) ובתמורה (דף כח.):
Rashi on Chullin 5a:10:4.english: A people similar to an animal - [Meaning,] who do not fulfill the commandments. Since [the word] "from," written with regard to an animal, [serves] to exclude one that engaged in bestiality [whether as the active or the passive party], so is it expounded in Bava Kamma (40b), Bechorot (41a), and Temurah (28a).

Rashi on Chullin 5a:10:5.hebrew: מפושעי ישראל - משמע מזידין, כדתניא במסכת יומא (דף לו:): פשעים אלו המרדים. וכן הוא אומר: מלך מואב פשע בי, והיינו מומר. ולקמן מפרש לה ואזיל:
Rashi on Chullin 5a:10:5.english: From the transgressors of Israel - This implies willful [sinners], as it is taught in tractate Yoma (36b): "transgressions" - these are rebellious acts. And so it says: "the king of Moab rebelled against me" [II Kings 3:7] - and this is [referring to] an apostate. And further on, [the Gemara] explains it.

Rashi on Chullin 5a:10:6.english: And pours the wine - For idol worship.

Rashi on Chullin 5a:13:1.english: If [it speaks of] an apostate with regard to one matter, the middle clause is difficult - Since it teaches, "we accept [an offering from him]," with regard to the last clause.

Rashi on Chullin 5a:14:1.hebrew: אלא לאו ה"ק - מקבלין קרבנות מפושעי ישראל במומר לדבר אחד, חוץ מן המומר לנסך את היין ולחלל שבתות, דהני חמירי, אלמא מומר לעבודת כוכבים כמומר לכל התורה כולה דמי. האי תנא חמירא ליה שבת כעבודת כוכבים, דהעובד עבודת כוכבים כופר בהקב"ה, והמחלל שבת כופר במעשיו ומעיד שקר שלא שבת הקב"ה במעשה בראשית:
Rashi on Chullin 5a:14:1.english: Rather, is this not what it is saying - We accept offerings from willful transgressors of Israel [in the case of] an apostate regarding one matter, except for one who is an apostate to pour libation wine [for idolatry] and to desecrate Sabbaths, for these are severe. This shows that an apostate to idol worship is considered like an apostate to the entire Torah. To this tanna, [desecrating the] Sabbath is as severe as idol worship, for one who worships idols denies the Holy One, blessed be He, while one who desecrates the Sabbath denies His deeds and testifies falsely that the Holy One, blessed be He, did not rest from the work of Creation.

Rashi on Chullin 5a:15:1.english: And is this derived from here? It is derived from there - [meaning] that we do not accept an offering from apostates.

Rashi on Chullin 5a:1:1.hebrew: לא הוה מפליג נפשיה מיניה - לא היה יהושפט נזהר ונבדל ממנו משום חשד כלל, אלמא אע"ג דמומר לעבודת כוכבים היה, לא הוי מומר לכל התורה כולה:
Rashi on Chullin 5a:1:1.english: He would not separate himself from him - Jehoshaphat was not at all careful to distance himself from him [Ahab] out of suspicion. This shows that even though he [Ahab] was an apostate regarding idol worship, he was not an apostate regarding the entire Torah.

Rashi on Chullin 5a:1:2.hebrew: כעמי כעמך - דמשמע הרי אתה כמותינו, דסומכין עלייהו:
Rashi on Chullin 5a:1:2.english: My people as your people - This implies: "You are indeed like us," meaning that they [your people] can be relied upon.

Rashi on Chullin 5a:1:3.hebrew: כסוסי כסוסיך ה"נ - דלענין איסור והיתר קאמר? אלא על כרחך לענין המלחמה קאמר ליה:
Rashi on Chullin 5a:1:3.english: Like your horses, so too here - Does he mean this with regard to [the laws of] forbidden and permitted [foods]? Rather, he must certainly mean it with regard to war.

Rashi on Chullin 5a:2:1.hebrew: בגורן - כי גורן היו יושבים בחיבה ובריעות ובאגודה א', כסנהדרין שאין חושדין זה את זה:
Rashi on Chullin 5a:2:1.english: At the threshing floor - Because at the threshing floor they would sit in affection, friendship, and unity, like the Sanhedrin, [whose members] do not suspect one another.

Rashi on Chullin 5a:2:2.hebrew: שיהו רואין זה את זה - להיות שומעין איש את חבירו, ומתווכחין זה עם זה, עד שתצא הוראה כהלכה. שאילו היו יושבין כשורה שלא בעגולה, אין בני ראש השורה רואין בני סוף שורתו. וכעגולה שלימה לא היו יושבין, כדי שיהא מקום לצאת ולבא:
Rashi on Chullin 5a:2:2.english: That they should see one another - So that they hear one another and debate with each other, until a correct ruling emerges. For if they sat in a row and not in a circle, those at the head of the row would not see those at the end of the row. And they would not sit in a complete circle, so that there would be room to go out and come in.

Rashi on Chullin 5a:3:2.hebrew: על פי הדבור שאני - שהקב"ה התירו לפי שעה, דכתיב (מלכים א יז) ואת העורבים צויתי שם לכלכלך:
Rashi on Chullin 5a:3:2.english: By the [divine] word it is different - for the Holy One, blessed be He, permitted it [only] temporarily, as it is written (I Kings 17): "and I have commanded the ravens to sustain you there."

Rashi on Chullin 5a:4:1.english: And the matter [just so] happened, etc. - [Said] as a rhetorical question.

Rashi on Chullin 5a:5:1.english: And perhaps [it is] after the name of their place - [meaning] that they [the ravens who fed Elijah] were from Tzur Orev (the Rock of Oreb).

Rashi on Chullin 5a:5:2.hebrew: מי לא כתיב - שאדם נקרא על שם מקומו, ואפילו יחיד, ואף ע"פ שאין מדבר בכל אנשי המקום, כגון פלשתים גבעונים, אלא באיש אחד, כדכתיב נערה קטנה:
Rashi on Chullin 5a:5:2.english: Is it not written - For a person is called by the name of his place, even a single individual, and even though it is not speaking of all the people of that place - such as [when Scripture says] "a Philistine" or "a Gibeonite" - but rather of one man alone, as it is written, "a young girl."

Rashi on Chullin 5a:5:3.hebrew: וקשיא לן קרי לה נערה - דהביאה ב' שערות, וקרי לה קטנה, דמשמע שלא הביאה שתי שערות:
Rashi on Chullin 5a:5:3.english: And it is difficult for us: it calls her a "na'arah" [maiden] - for she brought forth two [pubic] hairs, yet [elsewhere] it calls her a "ketanah" [minor], which implies that she did not bring forth two hairs.

Rashi on Chullin 5a:5:4.hebrew: וא"ר פדת - האי נערה לאו נערה ממש, אלא על שם מקומה, דמן נעורן. וה"נ, אע"ג דלאו בכל בני המקום קאמר, שהרי ודאי לכולן לא גילה, שהרי נחבא היה, מ"מ איכא למימר דתרי גברי הוו, וקראן על שם מקומן, ואין מזכיר שמם:
Rashi on Chullin 5a:5:4.english: And R. Pedat said - This "na'arah" [young woman] is not literally a young woman, but rather [she is called so] after the name of her place, for she was from Na'aran. And so too here [regarding the ravens] - even though it does not say that [Elijah] spoke to all the people of the place, for he certainly did not reveal himself to all of them, since he was in hiding - nevertheless, one can say that there were two men, and they were called by the name of their place, without their [actual] names being mentioned.

Rashi on Chullin 5a:5:5.english: Orebites [orviyyim] should have been written - so that one would not come to mistakenly think [the verse refers to] actual ravens.

Rashi on Chullin 5a:6:1.english: He is a full-fledged Jew - because he is one who is under duress [and so his failure to be circumcised is not held against him].

Rashi on Chullin 5a:7:1.hebrew: אי נימא מומר לדבר אחד - לאחד מכל המצות, לאשמועינן דלא הוה מומר לכל התורה כולה:
Rashi on Chullin 5a:7:1.english: If we say [it means] an apostate for one matter - [i.e.,] for one of all the mitzvot, [this comes] to teach us that he was not an apostate for the entire Torah.

Rashi on Chullin 5a:8:1.hebrew: שכל הכופר בה כמודה בכל התורה - כדכתיב (במדבר טו) וכי תשגו ולא תעשו את כל המצות האלה וגו', וילפינן בהוריות (דף ח.) דבעבודת כוכבים מיירי:
Rashi on Chullin 5a:8:1.english: For anyone who denies it is as though he acknowledges the entire Torah - As it is written (Numbers 15): "And if you shall err, and not observe all these commandments," etc., and we derive in [tractate] Horayot (8a) that it is speaking of idol worship.

Rashi on Chullin 5a:9:1.hebrew: מומר לאותו דבר - לשחיטה ולתיאבון, ואיצטריך לאשמועינן דלא תימא כיון דדש ביה כהיתירא דמי ליה, אלא ודאי כאיסורא דמי ליה, ולתיאבון הוא דעבר עליה, וכי מזמנינן ליה סכין לא שביק היתירא ואכיל איסורא:
Rashi on Chullin 5a:9:1.english: An apostate regarding that matter - [meaning] regarding [improper] slaughter, and out of desire [rather than spite]. And it was necessary to teach us this, lest you say: since he is habituated in it, it is as though it were permitted to him. Rather, [no,] it is certainly regarded by him as forbidden, and it is out of desire that he transgresses it. And when we present him with a [proper] knife, he would not leave the permitted [meat] and eat the forbidden.

Tosafot on Chullin 5a:10:1.hebrew: מכם ולא כולכם להוציא את המומר - תימה, דהא איצטריך לכדדרשינן בריש לולב הגזול (סוכה דף ל.): אי לפני יאוש, "אדם כי יקריב מכם" אמר רחמנא, והאי לאו דידיה הוא. וי"ל, דהתם לאו משום דתיפוק לן מהאי קרא גזול לפני יאוש, דהאי מביתו נפקא, כדאמרינן במרובה (ב"ק דף סז:): "קרבנו" ולא הגזול, אימת? אילימא לפני יאוש, ל"ל קרא? כלומר וכי יכול להקדיש? ביתו אמר רחמנא. ולא מייתי התם קרא דכי יקריב, אלא לומר דקרבן אמר רחמנא, והאי לאו קרבן הוא, שאין בידו להקדישו לפני יאוש. ועוד י"ל, דתרתי שמעינן ממכם, ולגזילה מקודשת איצטריך, ומביתו לא נפקא אלא שלא עלתה לשם חובה:
Tosafot on Chullin 5a:10:1.english: "From you" (mikem) - and not "all of you" - to exclude the apostate - This is puzzling, for this word is needed for the derivation made at the beginning of [the chapter] "Lulav HaGazul" (Sukkah 30a): [There the Gemara asks,] granted, before despair (yi'ush) [the owner has of recovering a stolen animal, a thief cannot sacrifice it, since] the Torah said, "when a man brings from you (mikem) an offering" - and this stolen animal is not his. [So "mikem" is used there to teach the exclusion of a stolen item - how then can it also teach the exclusion of the apostate here?] And one may answer: there, it is not because we derive that a stolen item [is excluded] before yi'ush from this verse ["mikem"] itself - rather, this is derived from [the requirement that an offering come] "from his own [domain]" (mibeito), as we say in [the chapter] "Merubah" (Bava Kamma 67b): "his offering" (korbano) - but not a stolen item. When [does this teaching apply]? If you say before yi'ush - why do I need a verse [to teach this]? That is to say, can he even consecrate it [when it is not yet his]? [It is obvious that] the Torah requires it to be "from his own [domain]" [without need for a special verse]. And there [in Bava Kamma], they do not cite the verse "when he brings... from you" [i.e. "mikem"], but rather [cite "korbano"] to say that the Torah calls it a "korban," and this [animal] is not a korban, since it was not in his power to consecrate it before yi'ush. And furthermore, one may answer: we learn two things from "mikem" - [the exclusion of the apostate,] and it is also needed for [the case of] a stolen item that has been consecrated; and this is not derived from "[from] his own [domain]," which teaches only that [such an offering] does not count toward fulfilling [the owner's] obligation [rather than that it is entirely invalid].

Tosafot on Chullin 5a:10:2.hebrew: כדי שיחזרו בהם בתשובה - לאו טעמא דקרא קא דריש, אלא נותן טעם לדבר, מדרבינן מהא מומר לדבר אחד טפי ממומר לכל התורה כולה, ולא מוקמינן קרא במילתא אחריתי. וקאמר דמומר לדבר אחד בקל יחזור בתשובה, ולכך מקבלין מהם כדי שיחזרו:
Tosafot on Chullin 5a:10:2.english: So that they may repent - [The Gemara] is not expounding the reason of the verse itself, but rather giving a reason for the matter, since we derive from this [verse] that an apostate (mumar) with regard to a single matter [is treated more leniently] than an apostate against the entire Torah, and we do not interpret the verse as referring to some other matter. And it states that an apostate with regard to a single matter will easily return in repentance (teshuvah), and therefore we accept [offerings] from them, so that they may repent.

Tosafot on Chullin 5a:3:1.hebrew: על פי הדבור שאני - וא"ת ולמאי דס"ד דלא הוי ע"פ הדבור, תקשי, דהא אמר רב: בשר שנתעלם מן העין אסור, לקמן (חולין דף צה.). ויש לומר דזה היה יודע שהיה סומך ע"פ הדבור דלאו משל עובד כוכבים קא מייתי, אבל לא ס"ד שבא הדבור להתיר האיסור שחיטת טבחים דאחאב:
Tosafot on Chullin 5a:3:1.english: By the word [of God], it is different - And if you will say: according to what we might have thought - that it was not by the word [of God] [that the ravens brought the food] - there is a difficulty, for Rav says below (Chullin 95a) that meat which has been out of sight is forbidden. And one can say: this one (Eliyahu) knew that he was relying on the fact that it was by the word [of God] that this was not brought from [the stock of] a non-Jew (oved kochavim). But it was not assumed that the word [of God] came to permit the prohibition of the slaughter of Achav's butchers.

Tosafot on Chullin 5a:5:1.hebrew: קרי לה נערה וקרי לה קטנה - בפרק בתרא דסוטה (דף מו:) דריש "נערים" שהיו מנוערים מן המצות, והכא לא שייך למדרש הכי:
Tosafot on Chullin 5a:5:1.english: It calls her a na'arah (young woman) and it calls her a ketanah (minor) - In the last chapter of Sotah (46b), it expounds [the word] "ne'arim" [in a verse] as [referring to] those who were "menu'arim" (shaken loose, i.e., exempted) from the mitzvot. But here, this homiletical reading does not apply.

Tosafot on Chullin 5a:5:2.hebrew: דמן נעורן - שם מקום, דכתיב (בד"ה א ז): "למזרח נערן ולמערב גזר":
Tosafot on Chullin 5a:5:2.english: Who was from Naaran - This is the name of a place, as it is written (I Chronicles 7:28): "and to the east, Naaran, and to the west, Gezer."

Tosafot on Chullin 5a:5:3.hebrew: עורביים מבעי ליה - ואף על גב דכתיב עברים מצרים ולא כתיב עבריים מצריים, התם ליכא למיטעי:
Tosafot on Chullin 5a:5:3.english: It should have said "oreviyim" [with a double yod] - Even though it is written "ivrim" [Hebrews] and "mitzrim" [Egyptians], and not "ivriyim" and "mitzriyim" [with a double yod], there, there is no possibility of confusion [since those words have no other meaning, so the plain form suffices]. [Here, by contrast, "orevim" already means "ravens," so if it meant "men of Orev," it would have to be written "oreviyim" to avoid being mistaken for ravens.]
